run.question:
I'm connected to the ci-cd cluster. We got a P1 alert and need help finding the root cause.
Our cluster inventory is in the app-235-cluster-inventory index and deployment/change history
is in the app-235-change-history index. Please search these indices to investigate.
[
  {
    "annotations": {
      "description": "Online Devices count gradual decrease over 8 hours in [clientorg-alpha] [56%] for over 30m",
      "workload": "clientorg-alpha"
    },
    "fingerprint": "xx1234567890abcd",
    "labels": {
      "alertname": "onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease",
      "app": "lambda-dashboard-monitoring",
      "cluster": "us-prod-eks",
      "grafana_dashboard_name": "Production-Performance-Overview",
      "org": "clientorg-alpha",
      "severity": "critical",
      "slack_channel": "sre-alerts-channel"
    },
    "startsAt": "30 minutes ago",
    "status": "firing"
  }
]
The alert started right after a deployment. Can you check what's the root cause?

report.summary: I could not tie the P1 (onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease, cluster us-prod-eks, org clientorg-alpha, app lambda-dashboard-monitoring) to any deployment or fault in the data this Run can reach. The change-history index contains only three changes inside the authorized 24h window, all for cluster ci-cd and all for CI/CD infrastructure (gitlab-runner scale 2->3 at 2026-11-21T03:22:12Z, argocd-server v2.9.2->v2.9.3 at 00:22:12Z, jenkins 2.426.2-lts->2.426.3-lts at 2026-11-20T23:22:12Z); the latest of these is about two hours before the window end (05:22:25Z), i.e. no recorded change coincides with an alert that started roughly 30 minutes before the report. The live Kubernetes target is an opspilot-m1 kind cluster whose namespaces are default, kube-*, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo; it does not contain the ci namespace or the jenkins/gitlab-runner/argocd-server workloads from the inventory, and its Prometheus configuration carries only CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh (cluster label opspilot-m1), OpsPilotAgentAbsent and OpsPilotModelCallsFailing - no online-devices rule. The only deployment seen being created recently is app-102b/traffic-manager (nginx:latest, 3/3 ready, restart count 0), created 2026-11-21T05:21:09Z, which postdates the alert onset and the window end, so it cannot be the trigger. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable for the whole Run (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no metric, error-rate, latency or trace evidence exists for the alerting workload; the root cause is not identified here.

claims.text: Inside the authorized window (2026-11-20T05:22:25Z to 2026-11-21T05:22:25Z) app-235-change-history returned exactly three change documents, all cluster=ci-cd and namespace=ci: BUILD-5PW2K6 gitlab-runner scale 2->3 at 2026-11-21T03:22:12Z, BUILD-3NR8Y1 argocd-server v2.9.2->v2.9.3 at 2026-11-21T00:22:12Z, BUILD-7X4Q9M jenkins 2.426.2-lts->2.426.3-lts at 2026-11-20T23:22:12Z.

Aggregations over the same window show only cluster=ci-cd (3 docs), namespace=ci (3 docs) and app_name buckets argocd-server, gitlab-runner, jenkins (1 each); change_type buckets are deployment (2) and scale (1). No other cluster or application is present in the window.
The most recent recorded change inside the 24h window is 2026-11-21T03:22:12Z, about two hours before the window end 2026-11-21T05:22:25Z; no change is recorded in the last two hours of the window.

app-235-cluster-inventory in the window holds three records, all cluster=ci-cd, namespace=ci, status=Running: argocd-server (quay.io/argoproj/argocd:v2.9.3, replicas 2, last_updated 2026-11-20T23:22:12Z), gitlab-runner (gitlab/gitlab-runner:v16.7.0, replicas 3, last_updated 2026-11-21T03:22:12Z), jenkins (jenkins/jenkins:2.426.3-lts, replicas 1, last_updated 2026-11-20T23:22:12Z).

The connected Kubernetes cluster's namespaces are default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo; there is no ci namespace and no namespace matching clientorg-alpha.

The deployments visible in the connected cluster are app-102b/traffic-manager, kube-system/coredns, kube-system/metrics-server, local-path-storage/local-path-provisioner and 21 otel-demo deployments (ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, jaeger, kube-state-metrics, load-generator, otel-collector, payment, product-catalog, prometheus, prometheus-readonly-proxy, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart); no jenkins, gitlab-runner or argocd-server workload exists there.

The Prometheus configuration held in ConfigMap otel-demo/prometheus defines only three alerting rules - CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh (labels cluster: opspilot-m1, severity: critical), OpsPilotAgentAbsent and OpsPilotModelCallsFailing - and contains no rule named onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease.

At 05:22:43Z all 35 pods returned across namespaces were phase Running with container ready=true; restart counts were 0 for most otel-demo pods and non-zero only for coredns (1), metrics-server (2), local-path-provisioner (2), kube-state-metrics (2) and prometheus-readonly-proxy (3).

otel-demo events in the window are cluster-startup events between 2026-11-21T04:23:46Z and 04:24:34Z (SandboxChanged, Created, Started for every pod) plus startup probe misses: kube-state-metrics-7cbf5b996-df4sz Unhealthy readiness (count 5) and liveness (count 2) connection refused plus BackOff (2); prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn Unhealthy readiness (5) plus BackOff (4); otel-collector-789c64b9bf-tl55c Unhealthy readiness (1).

The previous container of pod prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn logged at 2026-11-21T04:24:10Z: 'nginx: [emerg] host not found in upstream "prometheus:9090" in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf:22', i.e. the read-only Prometheus proxy failed to start because the prometheus upstream name did not resolve.

Deployment app-102b/traffic-manager (nginx:latest, app=nginx, replicas 3) reports creationTimestamp 2026-11-21T05:21:09Z with conditions Available/MinimumReplicasAvailable and Progressing/NewReplicaSetAvailable at 05:21:11Z, and 3 ready replicas.

The app-102b/traffic-manager pods observed at 05:23:49Z were traffic-manager-585c5579f6-5bcwl, -9whbx and -lcr2l, all Running/ready with restartCount 0 and startTime 2026-11-21T05:23:29Z, owned by ReplicaSet traffic-manager-585c5579f6 which itself reports creationTimestamp 2026-11-21T05:23:29Z and owner Deployment/traffic-manager. Earlier at 05:22:43Z the same workload's pods were named -fl4g2, -n4mdx and -pc94x, so this workload was being re-created between queries.

Every fault-injection flag in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad) has defaultVariant 'off', so no flagd fault is enabled in the configuration read.

The single node opspilot-m1-control-plane reports Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure False, 32859944Ki allocatable memory and a 110-pod capacity, and all 35 pods observed are Running and ready - no node- or pod-level resource shortage is visible in the connected cluster.

H: one of the recorded ci-cd changes caused the alert. Rejected on the evidence available: the latest recorded change is 2026-11-21T03:22:12Z, roughly two hours before the window end and therefore not 'right before' an alert that started about 30 minutes before the report; it is a scale-up of gitlab-runner from 2 to 3 replicas (a capacity increase), and the other two changes are an ArgoCD security patch and a Jenkins LTS bump, none of which is recorded as touching an online-device or clientorg-alpha workload.

H: the app-102b/traffic-manager deployment is the deployment the reporter refers to. Rejected: it was created at 2026-11-21T05:21:09Z (ReplicaSet and pods at 05:23:29Z), after both the alert onset (~30 minutes before the 05:22:25Z window end) and the window end itself, and all three of its pods are ready with restart count 0, so it shows no failure that could be the alert's cause.

The alert most likely did not originate from the environment reachable in this Run: its labels name cluster us-prod-eks, org clientorg-alpha and app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, while the connected target is an opspilot-m1 kind cluster containing only otel-demo and app-102b workloads, and its Prometheus configuration contains no onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease rule (only rules labelled cluster opspilot-m1). A mis-routed/foreign alert is consistent with every observation, but the us-prod-eks account is not inspectable here.

The alert's own description ('Online Devices count gradual decrease over 8 hours ... for over 30m') describes a trend that began about 7.5 hours before the alert fired, so a deployment made in the 30 minutes before firing could not by itself produce an 8-hour gradual decline; this needs confirmation from the clientorg-alpha online-device series, which is not available in this Run.

The app-102b/traffic-manager workload (namespace absent from the cluster's namespace list, Deployment created 05:21:09Z, ReplicaSet and pods re-created at 05:23:29Z, pod names replaced between successive queries) is being repeatedly re-applied by something outside this cluster's own controllers; its ownership chain is Deployment traffic-manager -> ReplicaSet traffic-manager-585c5579f6 -> pods, but what re-creates it is not visible in this Run. It postdates the alert and shows no failure.

Retrieve the clientorg-alpha online-device time series and the deployment/change record from the us-prod-eks account (Grafana Production-Performance-Overview and app lambda-dashboard-monitoring); nothing in the reachable sources carries that cluster, org, app or metric.

Restore the Prometheus/Jaeger read path before drawing metric conclusions: the prometheus-readonly-proxy container previously died with 'host not found in upstream "prometheus:9090"' and every Prometheus and Jaeger call in this Run returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.

Reconcile the CMDB with reality: the inventory/change-history indices record cluster ci-cd with namespace ci workloads (jenkins, gitlab-runner, argocd-server) that do not exist in the connected cluster, and record no change for the app-102b/traffic-manager deployment that does exist.

gaps: All Prometheus calls in this Run (get_metric_names, get_series, execute_prometheus_instant_query, list_prometheus_rules) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, and all Jaeger calls (traces_list_services, traces_list_operations, traces_search) also returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE; therefore no error-rate, latency, ERROR-series or trace evidence exists for any service, and missing error data is unknown, not zero.

No accessible source contains cluster us-prod-eks, org clientorg-alpha, app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, workload clientorg-alpha, or a metric/rule named onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease; the exact entity named in the alert has no data here.

app-235-change-history holds 4 documents in total but only 3 lie inside the authorized 24h window; the fourth document's timestamp and content are unknown because the tool's time filter cannot be removed (I queried timestamp 2026-11-20T05:22:25Z to 2026-11-21T05:22:25Z).
app-235-cluster-inventory holds 6 documents in total but only 3 lie inside the window; the other three records are unknown (last_updated filter 2026-11-20T05:22:25Z to 2026-11-21T05:22:25Z).

The inventory/change-history rows describe namespace ci workloads (jenkins, gitlab-runner, argocd-server) that do not exist in the connected cluster, while the connected cluster has an app-102b namespace that does not appear in its namespace list; which live cluster is the 'ci-cd' cluster of the alert remains unknown, and the namespace list and the pod list disagree.

What re-creates the app-102b/traffic-manager Deployment/ReplicaSet/pods every couple of minutes is not visible (Deployment created 05:21:09Z, ReplicaSet and pods 05:23:29Z, pod names replaced between 05:22:43Z and 05:23:49Z); it is after the alert window and shows no failure, so it cannot be placed as impact on the alert.

The alert's own timing (startsAt '30 minutes ago') and the 8-hour trend in its annotation were not verified against any monitoring source; the change_history integration is also listed as not_integrated in this Run, so no deployment pipeline record beyond the indexed documents can be checked.
No CronJob or Job objects were returned for the cluster (queries returned no data), so whether a one-off CI job ran near the alert onset is unknown rather than absent.

data.alertmanager.yml:
global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:
        [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] /etc/alertmanager/opspilot/token
        type: Bearer [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] ${env:PROMETHEUS_COLLECTOR_PASSWORD}
      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000

data.prometheus.yml:

  evaluation_interval: 1m
  scrape_interval: 1m
  scrape_timeout: 10s

data.alerting_rules.yml:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
